decisive_items: two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle
severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
response.rationale: The pathognomonic finding of both great vessels arising from the right ventricle confirms double outlet right ventricle (DORV). Other findings like septal defects and hypoplastic left ventricle are associated anomalies, not the primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Tetralogy of Fallot features overriding aorta, not both great vessels arising from the right ventricle; the described origin of both great vessels rules it out.
Ebstein's anomaly is characterized by apical displacement of the tricuspid valve, not described here; the key vascular origin finding is absent.
Tricuspid regurgitation is a secondary finding, not the underlying congenital malformation.
Atrial septal defect is one of the septal defects present but does not explain the origin of both great vessels.
Ventricular septal defect is present but is a component of the complex lesion, not the primary diagnosis.
Tricuspid atresia would show a hypoplastic right ventricle and absent tricuspid flow, opposite to the findings of right ventricular dilation and tricuspid regurgitation.
